speaker_role: independent counselor (InGenius Prep graduate coach/writer, interviewed by a podcast host from the same company); note company also sells admissions consulting services
commercial_incentive: yes - InGenius Prep is an admissions consulting company; episode promotes free consultations and the company's counselors/blog
key_insights: Recommends selecting summer programs with genuine selectivity, ideally field-specific, and favoring ones producing a tangible output (manuscript, research, startup) over lecture-only formats.

Advises against general pre-college 'campus experience' programs (e.g., generic summer-at-X classes) being a student's only summer activity, since they show less initiative/selectivity than competitive specialized programs.
Warns that an independent, self-directed project can demonstrate more initiative than getting into an overcrowded, easy-admit summer program.
Says it's not worth applying to 'safety' summer programs with high acceptance rates; time is better spent elsewhere.
Recommends referencing summer programs specifically in the activities list (using precise position titles and quantitative outcomes) and in supplemental 'why this school' essays when relevant.

Suggests roughly up to two summer programs across high school is a reasonable number, concentrated in freshman/sophomore years, with junior/senior time better spent on sustained leadership or self-initiated projects.
Notes early-decision-style early deadlines for summer programs (e.g., Yale Young Global Scholars) may be less competitive since fewer students have finished testing/materials by then.
specific_numbers_or_facts: Yale Young Global Scholars (YYGS): cited cost $6,500 for a two-week session; regular deadline stated as January 10, 2023.

notable_or_distinctive: Provides a specific, program-by-program cost and deadline rundown (rather than general advice) across general, STEM, humanities, and business categories, including which are most vs. least selective relative to price.
reliability_notes: Costs and deadlines were current as of this video's publication (~3 years old per manifest) and likely outdated now; speaker works for a paid admissions consulting company (InGenius Prep), which is a commercial incentive; some numbers (e.g., Wharton upper cost bound) appear garbled in the auto-caption transcript.
